items.title: Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1): corner charts and corner structures

book.label: §4.1, Definition 4.1.1 (preprint 4.1), p. 175 (preprint p. 147)
book.statement: An M-polyfold $X$ has a compatible smooth manifold structure with boundary with corners if it admits an atlas of sc-smoothly compatible charts $(V, \varphi, (U, C, \mathbb R^n))$, $\varphi : V \to U$ an sc-diffeomorphism from an open $V \subseteq X$ onto a relatively open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$ in $\mathbb R^n$ (or in a finite-dimensional vector space).

lean.statement: A corner chart (`MChart.IsCornerChart`) is a chart whose model is $(U, C, V)$ with $V$ finite-dimensional, the constant sc-structure, $U$ relatively open in the partial quadrant $C$, and the identity retraction. `HasCornerStructure`: an atlas of corner charts equivalent to the atlas of $X$; equivalently every point lies in a corner chart that is a chart of $X$. The dimension may vary. Corner models are tame retracts and sc⁺-retracts; a corner structure makes $X$ tame.

diff: "Sc-smoothly compatible" and "$\varphi$ an sc-diffeomorphism" are read as compatibility with the atlas of $X$, as for tameness (Findings, Chapter 4, item 50).
The classical manifold structure is represented by the corner atlas; local constancy of the dimension is neither stated nor formalized.

(2026-11-09) With the dimension fixed (`HasCornerStructureOfDim P n`), a corner structure gives a Mathlib `ChartedSpace (EuclideanQuadrant n)` with `IsManifold (modelWithCornersEuclideanQuadrant n) ∞`, and `IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞` without boundary (`cornerChartedSpace`, `isManifold_cornerChartedSpace`, `isManifold_interiorChartedSpace`); the partial quadrants of the charts are translated into the full quadrant, since a Mathlib manifold has one model (`Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge.lean`; gap G.102).

book.statement: A finite-dimensional Banach space $E$ has precisely one sc-structure, namely the constant structure $E_m = E$.

items.title: Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): $1_1^0$, $1_0^1$, and the constant structure

book.label: §4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)
book.statement: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ has the inverse $1_1^0$, which is always sc-smooth; so if $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth it is an sc-diffeomorphism. It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the underlying sets agree. A finite-dimensional space with the constant structure has $X = X^1$.

lean.statement: $1_1^0 : X^1 \to X$ is sc-smooth (in charts the sc-operator $\iota : E^1 \to E$). If $X = X_1$ as sets and $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth, it is an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $1_1^0$. For a finite-dimensional $V$: $(\mathrm{const}\,V)^1 = \mathrm{const}\,V$, the lift is the identity, every retract is an sc⁺-retract. **The example** (`remark_4_1_3_example`): an M-polyfold with $X_0 = X_\infty$ for which $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is not sc-smooth, so $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds; it is a retract $O = O_\infty \subseteq \mathbb R \oplus X$ that is not an sc⁺-retract (`remark_4_1_3_retract_example`), the image of the retraction $(t, z) \mapsto (t, L(t)z)$ of moving rank-one projections on a weighted sequence space, sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss (`IsLossFamily.isScSmooth`). $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (`MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff`).

diff: “It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the sets agree” is proved by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give (fourth addendum of this page; formerly gap G.31); the 2021 edition (p. 176) gives a different one, the space of its Subsection 1.4.4, which is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). By Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8) an example is a retract $O = O_\infty$ that is not an sc⁺-retract; it cannot come from a retraction whose level maps are $C^1$ (an argument, not formalized), so its retraction loses a level in its first derivative, as the splicings of HWZ do, and its sc-smoothness rests on a criterion with loss proved for it, not on Proposition 1.2.4 (preprint 1.19). In the example $X$ and $X^1$ even have different topologies on the same set (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

“$X^1 \ne X$” is read as “$1_0^1$ is not sc-smooth”, equivalently (by `remark_4_1_3_isScDiffeo`) “the identity is not an sc-diffeomorphism $X \to X^1$”. The sc-diffeomorphism clause needs only $X = X_1$, not $X_0 = X_\infty$. “$(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$” misprints $X_0$; $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ holds as sets and with the topologies of the iterated levels (`MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, V2.93; gap G.6, closed) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 5, 125). Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the missing example).

items.title: Lemma 4.5.1 on M-polyfolds: sc-smooth maps relate brackets

book.label: Appendix 4.5, Lemma 4.5.1, p. 201
book.statement: (New in the 2021 edition; the proof is left to the reader.) For a local sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi : X \to X$ and sc-smooth vector fields with $T\varphi(A(x)) = A(\varphi(x))$ and $T\varphi(B(x)) = B(\varphi(x))$ at points of $X_2$, $T\varphi([A, B](x)) = [A, B](\varphi(x))$ for $x \in X_2$.

notFormalized.book: If $X_0 = X_\infty$, then $X_m = X_0$ as sets for all $m$; "however, it is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as sc-smooth spaces despite the fact that $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$ as sets".

notFormalized.title: Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25): sc-differential forms and the directed system
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25), p. 195 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: An sc-differential $k$-form is an sc-smooth $\omega : \oplus^kTX \to \mathbb R$, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric; pull-back along $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ gives a directed system with limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09; V4.80–V4.82), in the chart-wise reading. A form is a family $\omega(x)$, $x \in X^1$, of alternating $k$-linear maps on the linear spaces $T_xX$ (gap G.7, closed), sc-smooth in the charts $\oplus_kT\varphi$ for every chart $\varphi$ of the maximal atlas; these are the charts the Whitney sum would have as an M-polyfold, and their transitions are sc-smooth (`IsScSmoothRetractMap.whitney`). A covering family of charts suffices (`isScForm_of_cover`). `MPolyfold.scForms` is $\Omega^k(X)$; the pull-back by $X^1 \to X$ (`formLower_mem_scForms`) gives the directed system (4.4) on the bundled lifts $X^i$ (gap G.6, closed), `BundledMPolyfold.formsInfty` is its direct limit $\Omega^k_\infty(X)$, a real vector space, and `formsInftyGraded` is $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$. $\oplus_kTX$ itself is not assembled into an M-polyfold bundle. The preprint writes $\Omega^*_\infty$ for both the limit and the sum; two names are used, as in the 2021 text (Findings, Chapter 4, items 124, 168).

notFormalized.title: Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26): the Lie bracket of sc-smooth vector fields
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196 (preprint p. 167)
notFormalized.book: (2021) For sc-smooth vector fields $A$, $B$ on $X$ the usual formula defines an sc-smooth section $[A, B]$ of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$, proved in Appendix 4.5 (§§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202). The preprint and 2017 texts state an sc-smooth vector field on $X^1$, a section of $T(X^1) \to X^2$, quoted from another paper.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (Springer 2021 additions; V4.74–V4.77), on an M-polyfold: $[A, B] : X^2 \to TX$, the bracket of the principal parts in any chart, is sc-smooth and covers the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$ (`proposition_4_4_5`, V4.76), independently of the chart (V4.75), by Lemma 4.5.1, whose proof the text leaves to the reader and which is proved by the computation of §4.5.2 in a local model (V4.74) and on M-polyfolds for every sc-smooth map (V4.77); the local model is V4.67–V4.72 (gap G.38, closed). "Section of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$" is read as a map $X^2 \to TX$ over the inclusion; the pull-back bundle itself and Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets are gap G.92. The sentence of p. 201 that the bracket at $x \in O_2$ lies on level $1$ does not hold as we read it (V4.73) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 155–157, 161, 162).

notFormalized.title: The exterior derivative, Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27) and the relative complex
notFormalized.label: §4.4, pp. 195–199 (preprint pp. 167–168), Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27)
notFormalized.book: $d : \Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^i)$ by the usual formula, $d^2 = 0$; $H^*_{sc}(X) = \ker d/\operatorname{im} d$; the relative complex $\Omega^*_\infty(X) \oplus \Omega^{*-1}_\infty(\partial X)$ with $d(\omega, \tau) = (d\omega, j^*\omega - d\tau)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09, 2026-11-10; V4.84–V4.88, V4.90, V4.91). The exterior derivative on an M-polyfold runs in the 2021 direction $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$, the direction item 120 proposed for the preprint: `MPolyfold.extD` is given in charts by the local formula $d(\omega_\varphi)$, does not depend on the chart (`extD_apply`), maps $\Omega^k(X)$ to $\Omega^{k+1}(X^1)$ (`extD_mem_scForms`) and is linear (`extDₗ`). $d \circ d = 0$ is proved (`extD_extD`, by the symmetry of the second derivative); $d$ commutes with $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ (`extD_formLower`) and passes to $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$ with $d^2 = 0$ (`formsInftyD`, `formsInftyGradedD_comp_self`); Definition 4.4.6 is `BundledMPolyfold.scDeRham`, read degree by degree. The formula of p. 197 holds with the sign $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ for the text's bracket; with the printed $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ it does not hold as we read it (V4.83). Forms on $\partial X$ are read through the tame boundary $B : bX \to X$ (Theorem 2.7.13): `bForms hP k i` $= \Omega^k(\partial X^i)$ are the sc-forms $\tau$ on $bX^i$ that agree over $B$ (on two local faces through a point the forms coincide on vectors with the same image in $TX$); the definition also lists the agreement of $d\tau$, which follows (2026-11-12; `isFaceCompatible_extD`, `bForms_eq_agreeForms`). $j^* = B^*$ (`jStar`, the pull-back of V4.89) with $dj^* = j^*d$ (`jStar_comp_D`); the relative complex `RelForms`, `relD` ($d(\omega, \tau) = (d\omega, j^*\omega - d\tau)$), `relD_comp_relD` ($d \circ d = 0$) and `relDeRham` ($H^k_{dR}(X, \partial X)$, degree by degree) (V4.90, V4.91). The agreement of $\tau$ implies that of $d\tau$ (`isFaceCompatible_extD`), so `bForms` is the set of agreeing sc-forms (`bForms_eq_agreeForms`) (Findings, Chapter 4, items 120–122, 167, 169, 170, 173).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28): Stokes' theorem
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28), p. 199 (preprint p. 168)
notFormalized.book: For an oriented compact tame smooth $n$-dimensional submanifold $N$ whose boundary is a union of faces $F$, and an sc-differential $(n - 1)$-form $\omega$, $\int_N d\omega = \sum_F\int_F\omega$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09, 2026-11-12; V4.92). Stokes' theorem is formalized for classical forms on Mathlib manifolds with boundary with corners. For a compact Hausdorff Mathlib manifold $M$ modelled on $[0, \infty)^{n+1}$ with a continuous tangent orientation $o$ (as Theorem 6.6.18 gives the solution sets, V6.61) and a $C^1$ $n$-form $\omega$ (`ManifoldForm`, `ContMDiffForm`), $\int_M d\omega = \int_{\partial M}\omega$ (`stokes_of_compactSpace`; `integral_extDeriv_eq_boundaryIntegral` for compact support). $d$ is Mathlib's exterior derivative read in charts, and does not depend on the chart (`ManifoldForm.chartForm_extDeriv`). $\int_M$ is defined through signed charts and a smooth partition of unity and does not depend on these choices (`IntegrationData.integral_eq`); the charts carry a sign since the quadrant model gives $[0, 1]$ no oriented atlas. $\int_{\partial M}$ is the sum of the face integrals in the charts, each face oriented outward vector first as in Definition 9.3.8 (`det_cons_neg_stdFrame_faceFrame`); for $C^1$ forms it does not depend on the choices (`IntegrationData.boundaryIntegral_eq`), the corners are a null set (`chartBoundaryIntegral_eq_sum_openQuadrant`), and chart changes preserve the faces and their induced orientation at the boundary points of degeneracy index $1$ (`exists_face_chartChange`, `orientation_face_chartChange`). The chart-level layer is Stokes' theorem on a quadrant and on a relatively open part of it (`stokes_quadrant`, `stokes_quadrant_inter_open`), with the change of variables $\int_{\varphi(s)}\omega = \pm\int_s\varphi^*\omega$ (`topFormIntegral_image_of_det_pos`, `topFormIntegral_image_of_det_neg`). Forms given only on the boundary are formalized (2026-11-09) as families of forms on the faces of the charts, smooth, compatible under chart changes and agreeing on the corners (`IsChartFaceForm`, `ChartFaceForm`). Every compactly supported one is the face restriction $j^*\beta$ of a smooth compactly supported form on $M$ (`exists_extension`, inclusion–exclusion in box charts glued by a partition of unity). Its integral over $\partial M$ is that of any extension (`ChartFaceForm.integral`, `faceIntegral_eq`), linear, with $\int_{\partial M} j^*\beta = \int_{\partial M} \beta$ (`ChartFaceForm.integral_ofForm`) and $\int_{\partial M} d\tau = 0$ (`ChartFaceForm.integral_d_eq_zero`). $d \circ d = 0$ holds for `ManifoldForm` (`ManifoldForm.extDeriv_extDeriv`) and on the faces (`ChartFaceForm.d_d`), with $j^*d = dj^*$ (`faceRestriction_extDeriv`). In dimension 0 the integral is a signed sum over the points (`ManifoldForm.integral_eq_sum_of_dim_zero`). (2026-11-09) For sc-forms: for a compact $S \subseteq X$ with a corner structure of dimension $n + 1$ (e.g. a compact submanifold in good position of a tame $X$), a continuous tangent orientation and $\omega \in \Omega^n_\infty(X)$, $\int_S (d\omega)|_S = \int_{\partial S} \omega|_S$ (`MPolyfold.stokes_formsInftyRestrict`, V4.92), with $\omega|_S$ the restriction of V4.92 and $\int_{\partial S}$ the boundary integral of the Mathlib manifold $S$ (outward vector first). On a product end $(a, b) \times N$ the boundary integral of $h(t)\,dt \wedge \beta_N$ is $-(\int h)\int_{\partial N} \beta_N$, also for face data (`ProductEnd.boundaryIntegral_end_sign`, `ProductEnd.faceIntegral_end_sign`). On a manifold with a product end, the pull-back of a form along the end projection is a smooth form after a cut-off, $d$ commutes with it, and an extension of face data can be glued from two ends (`ProductEnd.pullAt`, `ProductEnd.IsEndPullback.extDeriv`, `exists_glued_extension`). (2026-11-12) The faces in their own right: a compact tame M-polyfold has finitely many faces (`finite_setOf_isFace`), and in a face-structured one a face is, near each of its points and in any chart modelled on a tame retract, exactly a coordinate face (`exists_face_eq_coordHyper`). For $S$ face-structured (Definition 2.5.10, the reading of "a union of smooth faces"), every face $F$ has a corner structure of dimension $n$ (`hasCornerStructureOfDim_face`, via the coordinate faces in corner coordinates, `CornerCoords.exists_faceData`), so it is a Mathlib manifold; the induced orientation, outward vector first, exists, is unique and continuous (`inducedOrientation`; the chart changes of the faces are the face restrictions of those of $S$, `FaceChartPair.chartChangeDeriv_face`); and $\sum_F \int_F \omega|_F = \int_{\partial S}\omega$ (`sum_integral_restrictForm_eq_boundaryIntegral`), so Theorem 4.4.7 holds as printed, with the sum over the faces (`MPolyfold.theorem_4_4_7_hyp`, V4.92). The face-structured hypothesis is satisfiable: it holds without boundary (`isFaceStructured_of_forall_degIndex_eq_zero`) and for the quadrants (`isFaceStructured_quadrant`). The preprint and 2017 formulas write $\int_M$ for $\int_N$; the 2021 text writes $\int_N$ (Findings, Chapter 4, items 123, 171, 172, 177).

notFormalized.title: 2021 §4.4 and Appendix 4.5: sc-differential forms, the exterior derivative, Stokes, the Poincaré lemma
notFormalized.label: §4.4 and Appendix 4.5, pp. 195–208 (2021)
notFormalized.book: Definitions 4.4.1–4.4.2 (forms on the Whitney sum $\oplus_kTX$, the direct limit $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$), the exterior derivative $d : \Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ with $d^2 = 0$, Definition 4.4.6 and the relative complex, Theorem 4.4.7 (Stokes), the Poincaré Lemma 4.4.8 (p. 199) and its local form Lemma 4.5.2 (p. 202, proved in §4.5.3).
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-09, 2026-11-12, 2026-11-13; continues G.37–G.40). Formalized: Definitions 4.4.1–4.4.2, with $\oplus_kTX$ read in its charts $\oplus_kT\varphi$ (gap G.37 closed, V4.80–V4.82); the exterior derivative on an M-polyfold, chart independent and linear, with $d^2 = 0$, commuting with the inclusions $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ and passing to $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$, and Definition 4.4.6 (V4.84–V4.88); the formula of p. 197, which holds with $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ for the text's bracket, while the printed $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ does not hold as we read it (V4.83); integration and Stokes' theorem for classical forms on compact oriented Mathlib manifolds with corners, and Theorem 4.4.7 with the sum over the faces (gap G.40, closed; V4.92). The vector fields of Definition 4.4.3, Lemma 4.4.4 (for every $i$), the bracket of Proposition 4.4.5 and Lemma 4.5.1 are formalized as before (V4.67–V4.79). (2026-11-09, 2026-11-10) Also formalized: the pull-back $f^*$ along an sc-smooth map of M-polyfolds, on $\Omega^k(X^i)$ and on $\Omega^k_\infty$, with $f^*d_Y = d_Xf^*$, functoriality and the induced map on $H^k_{sc}$ (V4.89); forms on $\partial X$, $j^*$, the relative complex and $H^*_{dR}(X, \partial X)$ (gap G.39 closed, V4.90–V4.91); the restriction of sc-forms to a finite-dimensional sub-M-polyfold $S$ with a corner structure of dimension $n$ as a Mathlib form on the manifold $S$, $C^\infty$ and commuting with $d$ and with the system (4.4) (`scFormRestrict`, `formsInftyRestrict`, `extDeriv_formsInftyRestrict`), and with it Theorem 4.4.7 for sc-forms (V4.92); the restriction of forms on $\partial X$ to the faces of a sub-M-polyfold $S$ with $d_S = d_X$ as forms on the faces of the Mathlib manifold $S$, with $\int_{\partial S} j^*\omega = \int_{\partial S} \omega|_S$ and $d$ commuting (`solFaceForm`, `solFaceForm_jStar_integral`, `solFaceForm_d`); forms on the faces of Mathlib manifolds with corners, their $d$ and their integral, with $\int_{\partial M} d\tau = 0$ (G.40); on a product end $(a, b) \times S$ of $S' \subseteq \mathbb R^1 \times X$, the restriction of $p_1^*\omega$ is the pull-back of $\omega|_S$ in the product charts (`isEndPullback_formsInftyRestrict_snd`), and an sc-smooth function on a finite-dimensional corner M-polyfold is $C^\infty$ on the Mathlib manifold (`contMDiff_of_isScSmoothMap_real`). (2026-11-12) Also formalized: the wedge product of sc-forms, read classically as $(a\wedge b)(v) = (k!\,l!)^{-1}\sum_\sigma \operatorname{sign}\sigma\, a(v_{\sigma(1..k)})\,b(v_{\sigma(k+1..k+l)})$ since the text uses it without a definition (`formWedge`, `formsInftyWedge`): it is bilinear, associative, graded commutative and unital, and satisfies the Leibniz rule (`extD_formWedge`, `formsInftyD_formsInftyWedge`); $\Omega^*_\infty(X) = \bigoplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X)$ is thereby a graded $\mathbb R$-algebra (`formsInftyGAlgebra`) on which $d$ is a derivation of degree $+1$ with $d^2 = 0$ (`formsInftyGradedD_of_mul_of`), the graded differential algebra of p. 198, and $f^*$ is a morphism of graded algebras (V4.87, V4.89); sc-forms on open subsets, with the restrictions $\Omega^k(X) \to \Omega^k(U)$ and $\Omega^k_\infty(X) \to \Omega^k_\infty(U)$ commuting with $d$ (`formRestrict`, `formsInftyResOpen`) and "$[\omega] = [\tau]$ on $V$" of (4.7) (`FormsInftyEqOn`, `formsInftyEqOn_of_iff`); the Poincaré Lemma 4.4.8 (`lemma_4_4_8`, V4.95) and its local form Lemma 4.5.2 for a convex relatively open $U \subseteq C$ (`hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`, `lemma_4_5_2`, V4.96), with the homotopy operator $\tau(y)(v) = \int_0^1 t^k\,\omega(c + t(y-c))(y-c, v)\,dt$ about a smooth centre $c$ ($c = 0$ in the text; Lemma 4.4.8 needs a general one, since $B_\delta(x) \cap C$ need not contain $0$), sc-smooth as a parametric integral (`isScSmooth_intervalIntegral`); the agreement of $d\tau$ for forms $\tau$ on $\partial X$ that agree (V4.90); the pull-back of forms on $\partial X$ to the faces of a finite-dimensional sub-M-polyfold $S$ of a second tame M-polyfold along an sc-smooth $G : S \to X$ with $d_S = d_X \circ G$, with $d$ commuting and $(G^*\eta)_S$ extending $(G^*j^*\eta)|_{\partial S}$ (`faceAlongData`, `faceAlongData_formsD`, `isExtendedBy_faceAlongData_formsPullback`), the case $G = p_1$ used for Theorem 6.7.1 (gap G.54). (2026-11-13; `Chapter4/GapP3_K4_BoundaryWedge.lean`, `GapP3_K4_RelWedge.lean`) The wedge product on the relative complex is formalized, so $\Omega^*_\infty(X, \partial X)$ is a differential algebra. On the forms on $\partial X$: the wedge product of agreeing forms is agreeing, and on $\Omega^*_\infty(\partial X)$ it is bilinear, associative and unital with the Leibniz rule (`agreeDFormsInftyWedge`, `agreeDFormsInftyD_agreeDFormsInftyWedge`, `agreeDFormsInftyWedge_assoc`); $j^*$ is multiplicative (`jStar_formsInftyWedge`). On $\Omega^*_\infty(X, \partial X)$ the text gives no product; our choice is the product of the mapping cone of $j^*$, $(\omega, \tau)(\omega', \tau') = (\omega\wedge\omega', (-1)^k j^*\omega\wedge\tau')$ for $(\omega, \tau)$ of degree $k$ (`relWedge`): $d$ is a derivation of degree $+1$ (`relD_relWedge`, `relGradedD_of_mul_of`) with $d^2 = 0$ (`relGradedD_comp_self`), the product is associative (`relWedge_assoc`, `relGraded_mul_assoc`), so $\bigoplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X, \partial X)$ is an associative ring (`relGradedNonUnitalRing`), and $(1, 0)$ is a unit on the left (`relCast_relWedge_relOne`) but not on the right (`relWedge_relOne`); the projection to $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$ is multiplicative (`relFst_relWedge`). The 2021 text of §4.4 (pp. 198–199) defines $f^*$ for sc-smooth maps of M-polyfolds (formalized, V4.89) and, on $\partial X$, only $j^*$ for the inclusion; it does not define a pull-back of forms on $\partial X$ along a general sc-smooth map. Such a pull-back is used only in the proof of Theorem 6.7.1, for $p_1$ on the faces of the solution set $S_F \subseteq \partial X\times[0, 1]$, and that use is formalized (`faceAlongData` above, gap G.54); the general pull-back is not formalized and no statement of Parts I–II depends on it (Findings, Chapter 4, items 158, 167–173, 177, 178).

notFormalized.title: Lemma 4.5.1 for local sc-diffeomorphisms between open subsets; the pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$
notFormalized.label: §4.4, Proposition 4.4.5, p. 196, and Appendix 4.5, Lemma 4.5.1, p. 201 (2021)
notFormalized.book: (New in the 2021 edition.) Lemma 4.5.1: a local sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi : X \to X$ that relates two vector fields relates their brackets. Proposition 4.4.5: the bracket is an sc-smooth section of the pull-back $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ of $TX \to X^1$ by the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V4.76, V4.77). Lemma 4.5.1 holds for every sc-smooth map $f : X \to Y$ (V4.77) and for maps between open subsets ($U, U'$ Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds, `lemma_4_5_1_open`, `lemma_4_5_1_open_ambient`; the bracket is local, `lieBracket_restrictOpen`), in particular for a local sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of $X$. The pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 = \{(x, \alpha) \in X^2 \times TX \mid p(\alpha) = x\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X^2 \times TX$ (`isSubMPolyfold_tangentPullback`), with sc-smooth projection to $X^2$ and fibres $T_xX$; $[A, B]$ is an sc-smooth section of it (`proposition_4_4_5_section`), and Lemma 4.5.1 holds for the sections with the bundle map $(f_2, Tf)$ (`lemma_4_5_1_section`). The text gives $TX|X^2$ no structure; the sub-M-polyfold structure is used (Findings, Chapter 4, item 163).
